newsitem.title: USA: Police continue probe in murder of Colorado child.
newsitem.headline: Police continue probe in murder of Colorado child.

text.p: Detectives in Colorado and Georgia on Sunday persisted in their painstaking search for the killer of a 6-year-old beauty pageant winner, the victim of a crime that has attracted national attention.
"There's an active and on-going investigation and certain aspects (of the probe) that are continuing," Kelvin McNeill, a spokesmen for the Boulder, Colorado, police department, said.
Public attention in Colorado and across the country has been riveted on the murder mystery.
The body of JonBenet Ramsey was found the day after Christmas in her family's 15-room home in a posh neighbourhood in Boulder, about 30 miles northwest of Denver.
A ransom note demanding $118,000 was found in the home by the mother as she came downstairs to make coffee.

The child's body was found by her father about eight hours later in a windowless room in a basement where Christmas presents had been stored. The blond, blue-eyed child was strangled and according to news reports her skull was fractured and she had been sexually assaulted, but police have remained tight lipped about aspects of the probe.
McNeill said police concluded their investigation at the crime site and returned the home to the parents, John and Patricia Ramsey, who remained in seclusion at an undisclosed location in Colorado.
Police also assembled an inventory list of items taken from the home, McNeill said.
The girl was buried last week in Georgia where the family lived before moving to Boulder in 1991.
Meanwhile, five Boulder detectives continued their investigation in Georgia, interviewing family and business associates of the Ramseys.
John Ramsey is chief executive of Access Graphics, a computer company in Boulder that was acquired in 1991 by the Lockheed Corp., now Lockheed Martin.
The mother, Patricia Ramsey, who has battled cancer, is a former Miss West Virginia who shepherded her daughter's fledgling career as a beauty pageant contestant.
Boulder police were also trying to set up a formal interview with the parents, who have both retained attorneys.
"We expect the family to continue to be cooperative. It's simply a matter of scheduling," McNeill said.

In an interview last week with CNN the parents, looking distraught and bewildered, denied any involvement in the murder and said they would assemble a private investigative team to find out what happened.

But many questions remain. The Rocky Mountain News has reported that a security system at the home was not on the night of the murder. Other published reports also said there did not appear to be a forced entry into the home and that the ransom note was written on paper taken from a pad found in the home.
The detectives dispatched to Georgia were expected to be back in Boulder for a debriefing by Monday night, McNeill said.

The murder has been the main topic on countless hours of talk radio and passersby have tied up traffic in front of the house where candy canes and other Christmas decorations remain, creating an eerie atmosphere.

Denver television station KCNC showed excerpts from a video taken in 1994, showing a fashionably decorated home. In the video a 4-year-old JonBenet looks like any typical child, a contrast to more recent pictures of her as a beauty queen wearing lipstick and a tiara.
